question: The Cyber and Information Domain Coordination Centre (CIDCC), a permanent structured cooperation project, has been providing essential cyber situational awareness, threat analysis, and operational support for EU missions since 2023.

In May 2023, the European Council reaffirmed its commitment to integrate the CIDCC into the EU Cyber Defence and Coordination Centre (EU CDCC) in 2025, a critical capability for European defence and strategic autonomy.

The European External Action Service (EEAS) has indicated that in 2026, no financial resources will be allocated for the establishment of the EU CDCC, raising serious concerns about the EU’s ability to maintain cyber and information resilience. In this context, the HR/VP is asked to clarify: 1.
Why has the EEAS not allocated adequate funding for the EU CDCC in 2026, despite the EEAS's acknowledgement of the strategic importance of the CDCC for EU missions and defence readiness?
How does the EEAS plan to safeguard the continuity of cyber situational awareness and operational support during the transition from the CIDCC prototype to the EU CDCC?
What concrete measures will the EEAS take to guarantee that the EU CDCC is established on time and is fully operational, ensuring Europe’s independence and resilience in the cyber domain?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.1.2026) The proposal for an EU Cyber Defence Coordination Centre (EU CDCC) was put forward in the EU Cyber Defence Policy1 in 2022, building on the Permanent Structured Cooperation (PESCO) project ‘Cyber and Information Domain Coordination Centre (CIDCC)’.

In 2023 the Council welcomed the work of CIDCC and the proposal to integrate it into the EU CDCC and called on the High Representative/Vice-President to present a concept for its establishment2. In 2024, the European External Action Service (EEAS) presented a concept note to Member States.

Based on the guidance received from Member States, the EEAS is working on progressively developing the EU CDCC as a permanent capability. The EU CDCC is envisaged to be the EU military cyber hub to facilitate and enhance military cyber situational awareness across the EU and its Member States.

Member States agreed to establish a nucleus that will focus on cyber situational awareness for EU military missions and operations. This nucleus is expected to facilitate the transition and transfer of knowledge from the CIDCC to the EU CDCC.

Within the currently existing EEAS budget constraints, the EEAS will set up an EU CDCC core nucleus based on reallocation of internal resources in view of ensuring the best possible arrangements to facilitate the transition from PESCO CIDCC in the first semester of 2026. Further development of the Centre is subject to a prioritisation exercise.
